_comment: The install, in the order you do it. Each group is one download and one instruction, and every row is a path
relative to the folder holding mgs4.exe. launcher/src/Checks.cs reads this and renders it as the Setup tab
the Setup tab and as --report, and its drag-and-drop uses 'accepts' to know what a dropped file is for.
Versions match the 'setup this was verified on' table in docs/install.md - change both together.
required        a missing file in this group is a failure; files[].optional and files[].required override it
url / urlLabel  where this group's files come from, as a button above them
guide           what to do with them, in the order it is done
accepts         file names this group takes by drag-and-drop; a .zip is unpacked into the game folder
bundled         this group's files ship with the app - built into the release exe - so Setup can install them itself (Install.BundledAddon)
drop            the headline file to drag in, named in the drop area; accepts is the full match list
files[].path    relative to the game folder - the row's label

sections.title: 1. The game
sections.blurb: Everything else goes in the folder this sits in.
sections.guide: Metal Gear Solid 4, Master Collection Vol. 2. In its options set Graphics -> API to DirectX 12, FXAA off, vsync off and the frame limiter to 60.

files.detail: one line holding 2492670. Neither Steam nor the game writes it: without it mgs4.exe is handed back to Steam at startup and relaunched without its arguments, which is how a --stage boot loses the stage. Launching a scene writes it, or press the button above.

sections.title: 2. ReShade, with add-on support
sections.blurb: The host this add-on loads into. The plain build looks identical on disk and silently loads nothing.
sections.guide: Drop the setup here and it installs itself: run headless against mgs4.exe, as dxgi.dll, with no shader packs - none are used. Download the build marked "with full add-on support"; the plain one looks identical on disk and silently loads nothing. Running the setup by hand still works: point it at mgs4.exe and pick the Direct3D 10/11/12 renderer.

files.detail: ReShade itself, under the name the game loads

sections.title: 3. DLSS and Streamline runtimes
sections.blurb: One zip holds all of these. nvngx_dlss.dll is what DLSS itself needs; the rest are for frame generation.
sections.guide: In the Discord's Pinned Messages, take the Streamline zip - named for the versions it carries, DLSS310.8.0-Streamline2.13.zip at the time of writing, streamline.zip in older pins - and extract everything in it straight into the folder with mgs4.exe. It carries the NVIDIA runtimes and the Streamline libraries together, already matched to each other - you do not need the NVIDIA or Streamline SDKs separately. If the NVIDIA app's DLSS override is on for this game it supplies nvngx_dlss.dll instead.

files.detail: DLSS Super Resolution - the one piece DLSS cannot run without
the Streamline entry point the add-on loads

sections.title: 4. DLSS 5 Neural Rendering add-on
sections.blurb: Optional. With this present the add-on runs DLAA on the final image, so NR works at full strength.
sections.guide: From the same Pinned Messages, take the newest renodx-dlss5.addon64 and drop it next to mgs4.exe. Nothing to configure: this add-on notices it and moves the DLAA pass to the composite on its own.

sections.title: 5. This add-on
sections.blurb: Last, so it loads with everything else already in place.
sections.guide: Install it from here - the add-on is built into this app, so there is nothing to download. Dropping mgs4_dlss.addon64 in by hand still works, as does dlss-addon\build.bat then sh dlss-addon/install.sh. The ini beside it is the configuration this was verified with; without it the add-on falls back to its built-in defaults.

files.detail: its settings; the first run writes the detected InternalRes into it
